objects: CpG sites; genomic annotations; regional DM
assumptions: 450K arrays include intergenic sites without gene annotation
conclusion: Pre-annotated regions restrict candidate probes for DMR detection and can bias results toward richly annotated genomic regions.
span: A possible biasing factor is that some genomic regions are more richly annotated than others, which may persuade researchers to concentrate on these at the expense of more enigmatic regions. Methods such as IMA[28] and COHCAP[29] use pre-annotated regions a priori, which comprise only a subset of the 450K probes as the primary backbone for DMR detection, biasing their results.

span: All the user needs to provide to the DMRcate workflow is an Illumina probe ID-indexed matrix of methylation measurements and, for DMR finding, a model matrix (optionally with an additional contrast matrix) reflecting the experimental design.

conclusion: The DMR options use limma linear models with selected factors, covariates, and variance shrinkage at each CpG.
span: Our method has three different analysis options. These correspond to the rows of Table 2. The first two options begin with standard linear modelling using limma[43], which uses selected factors and covariates, and variance shrinkage, to fit a linear model to all CpG sites in parallel.

conclusion: Local statistics are Gaussian-smoothed over ordered CpG genomic coordinates separately for each chromosome.
span: We now smooth the statistics Yi at the locations xi with a Gaussian smoother. This and the other steps below are done separately for each chromosome. Let x1<⋯<xn be the CpG sites for the current chromosome.

assumptions: known numerator and denominator degrees of freedom
conclusion: Each local statistic Yi is assumed to follow an F distribution with known mu and nu before modeling the smoothed statistic.
scope: Local-statistic distribution, not a joint likelihood for methylation measurements
span: Each Yi is assumed to be an F statistic with (μ,ν) degrees of freedom where μ and ν are known values (see Table 2). We now model the distribution of SKY(i).

objects: F denominator; nu; local scaled chi-squared approximation
assumptions: nu is large so each F denominator is close to one
conclusion: The method approximates local F statistics by taking their denominators to be close to one for large nu.
scope: Intermediate approximation used before modeling the smoothed statistic
span: We take an intermediate approach in which we assume ν is large so that the denominator in each F statistic is close to one.

objects: SKY(i); scaled chi-squared random variable; first two moments
assumptions: large-nu approximation for local F statistics
conclusion: Satterthwaite moment matching approximates the smoothed statistic by a scaled chi-squared variable whose scale and degrees of freedom match its first two moments.
scope: Approximate null distribution of the smoothed statistic
span: With this assumption we use the approximation of Satterthwaite [65], in which we model SKY(1) by a scaled chi-squared random variable, , where the constants ai and bi are chosen to match the first two moments.

objects: Pi; BH-adjusted Qi; lambda; region boundaries
assumptions: retain sites below a selected adjusted-P threshold
conclusion: BH-adjusted site P values are thresholded, then retained CpGs separated by at most lambda are collapsed into regions.
scope: Site-level adjustment and region construction; this sentence supplies no region-level FDR theorem
span: We then perform a BH correction [68] on the P values Pi, giving adjusted P values, Qi, and retain the subset of CpG sites xi where Qi is smaller than a given threshold (usually 0.05). Finally, regions (DMRs or VMRs, depending on the analysis option) are defined by collapsing groups of the remaining CpG sites that are at most λ nucleotides from each other.

objects: kernel support; small true DMRs; false positives
assumptions: very small true DMRs in the discussed subtle-effect comparison
conclusion: Kernel support can infer false differential methylation beyond small true DMRs, an effect the authors say can be reduced by shrinking the kernel.
scope: Author explanation of observed behavior, not a general error bound
span: At this point, DMRcate likely incurs more false positives due to kernel support inferring false DM beyond the flanks of these very small true DMRs, as seen with the simulated data. However, this effect can be minimised by shrinking the kernel size (Figure 4b).
